chapterInsights.title: Python Basics & Environment
outcomes: Install Python and set up a development environment (Anaconda/VS Code)
Write and execute basic Python scripts
Understand the difference between script mode and interactive mode
Use print() and basic input/output

definitions.definition: Integrated Development Environment — a software application that provides tools for writing, testing, and debugging code (e.g., VS Code, PyCharm, Jupyter Notebook).
A program that executes Python code line-by-line at runtime, rather than compiling to machine code first.
A Python file (ending in .py) containing a sequence of instructions to be executed.
The set of rules that define the structure and format of valid Python statements.

revisionPrompts: What is the purpose of an IDE in Python development?
How do you run a Python script from the command line?
What does the print() function do?
What is the difference between interactive mode and script mode?
chapterInsights.saContext: NWU BCom students typically use Anaconda with Jupyter Notebooks or VS Code as their Python environment. Python is increasingly used in South African business analytics contexts, including financial modelling and data reporting.

chapterInsights.title: Data Types & Variables
outcomes: Identify Python's core data types: int, float, str, bool
Declare and assign variables following naming conventions
Perform type conversion using int(), float(), str()
Use string methods and formatting

definitions.definition: A named storage location in memory that holds a value which can change during program execution.
A classification of data that determines what operations can be performed on it (e.g., int, float, str, bool).
Converting a value from one data type to another using functions like int(), float(), or str().
A sequence of characters enclosed in single or double quotes, used to represent text.

revisionPrompts: What are the four primitive data types in Python?
How do you convert a string '42' to an integer?
What will type('hello') return?
How do you concatenate two strings in Python?
chapterInsights.saContext: Understanding data types is fundamental for processing South African business data such as rand amounts (float), customer IDs (int or str), and boolean flags in business rule systems.

chapterInsights.title: Control Flow
outcomes: Write conditional logic using if, elif, and else
Implement for loops to iterate over sequences
Use while loops for condition-based repetition
Apply break, continue, and pass statements

definitions.definition: A programming construct (if/elif/else) that executes different code blocks based on whether a condition is True or False.
The process of repeating a block of code multiple times using a loop.
A statement that exits a loop immediately before its natural termination condition.
A built-in Python function that generates a sequence of numbers, commonly used with for loops.

revisionPrompts: What is the syntax for an if-elif-else statement in Python?
How does a for loop differ from a while loop?
What does the break statement do inside a loop?
How would you print numbers 1 to 10 using a for loop?
chapterInsights.saContext: Control flow structures are used in business logic programming, such as applying VAT conditionally on South African transactions or iterating through customer records to calculate balances.

chapterInsights.title: Functions & Modules
outcomes: Define and call functions with parameters and return values
Understand variable scope (local vs global)
Import and use built-in Python modules
Create simple custom modules

definitions.definition: A named, reusable block of code that performs a specific task, optionally accepting inputs (parameters) and returning a result.
A variable listed in a function's definition that receives a value when the function is called.
The value a function sends back to the caller using the return statement.
A Python file containing functions, classes, and variables that can be imported and used in other scripts.
The region of code where a variable is accessible. Local variables exist only within a function; global variables are accessible throughout.

revisionPrompts: How do you define a function in Python?
What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
How do you import the math module?
What does the return statement do?
chapterInsights.saContext: Functions promote code reusability, which is essential in business data processing tasks such as repeatedly calculating tax (15% VAT) or formatting South African rand values.

chapterInsights.title: Data Structures (Lists/Dicts/Sets)
outcomes: Create and manipulate Python lists using indexing and methods
Build and access dictionaries using key-value pairs
Use sets for unique collections and set operations
Understand when to use each data structure

definitions.definition: An ordered, mutable collection of items enclosed in square brackets, allowing duplicate values.
An unordered collection of key-value pairs enclosed in curly braces, accessed via unique keys.
An unordered collection of unique items, useful for removing duplicates and set operations like union and intersection.
The position of an element in a list, starting from 0 for the first element.
A pair of associated data in a dictionary where the key is a unique identifier and the value is the associated data.

revisionPrompts: How do you access the third element of a list?
How do you add a new key-value pair to a dictionary?
What is the difference between a list and a set?
How do you remove duplicates from a list using a set?
chapterInsights.saContext: Data structures are used to organise business data such as lists of product prices, dictionaries of customer details, and sets of unique transaction IDs in South African retail analytics.

chapterInsights.title: File I/O & Data Handling
outcomes: Open, read, and write text files using Python's open() function
Read and write CSV files using the csv module and Pandas
Handle exceptions using try/except blocks
Validate and clean basic input data

definitions.definition: Input/Output operations involving reading data from and writing data to files on disk.
Comma-Separated Values — a plain text file format where each line represents a record and values are separated by commas.
A mechanism using try/except blocks to catch and handle runtime errors gracefully without crashing the program.
A Python construct using the 'with' statement that automatically handles resource management such as closing files.

outcomes: Create and manipulate Pandas Series and DataFrames
Filter, sort, and index data in a DataFrame
Perform groupby operations and aggregation
Handle missing data using fillna() and dropna()

definitions.definition: A two-dimensional, labelled data structure in Pandas, similar to a spreadsheet or SQL table, with rows and columns.
A one-dimensional labelled array in Pandas, representing a single column of data.
A Pandas operation that splits data into groups based on a column value, applies a function, and combines the results.
The row labels of a Pandas DataFrame or Series, used for fast data access and alignment.
Not a Number — a special floating-point value used in Pandas to represent missing or undefined data.

outcomes: Create line, bar, and scatter plots using Matplotlib
Customise plots with titles, axis labels, legends, and colours

definitions.definition: A Python library for creating static, animated, and interactive data visualisations.
The entire chart window or image area in Matplotlib, which can contain one or more subplots.
An individual plot area within a Matplotlib figure, containing the chart elements such as lines, bars, and labels.
A guide on a chart that explains what each line, bar, or marker represents.

flashcards.front: What is an IDE?
flashcards.back: An Integrated Development Environment — software that provides tools for writing, testing, and debugging code. Examples include VS Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter Notebook.

flashcards.front: How do you print text to the screen in Python?
flashcards.back: Use the print() function. Example: print('Hello, World!')

flashcards.front: What file extension do Python scripts use?
flashcards.back: .py — for example, my_script.py

flashcards.front: What is Anaconda?
flashcards.back: A Python distribution that includes Python, package manager (conda), and popular data science libraries pre-installed. It is commonly used in academic and data analysis environments.

flashcards.front: What is a comment in Python and how do you write one?
flashcards.back: A comment is a line of code ignored by the interpreter, used to explain code. Single-line comments start with #. Example: # This is a comment

quizItems.prompt: Which of the following is a Python IDE commonly used for data analysis?
quizItems.explanation: Jupyter Notebook is a widely used IDE for data analysis in Python, allowing code, text, and visualisations in a single document.

quizItems.prompt: What is the correct Python syntax to display 'Hello' on screen?
quizItems.explanation: The print() function is Python's built-in function for outputting text to the console.

quizItems.prompt: Python scripts are saved with which file extension?
quizItems.explanation: Python source code files use the .py extension, e.g., analysis.py.

workedExamples.title: First Python Script
workedExamples.summary: Writing and running a simple Python script that prints a greeting.
workedExamples.problem: Write a Python script that prints your name and the current module code.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Open your IDE (e.g., VS Code or Jupyter Notebook).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Create a new file called greeting.py.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Type the following code: print('My name is Lottie') followed by print('Module: CMPG222')

steps.label: Step 4

workedExamples.answer:
My name is Lottie

flashcards.front: What are the four basic data types in Python?
flashcards.back: int (integers), float (decimal numbers), str (text strings), and bool (True/False values).

flashcards.front: How do you convert the string '100' to an integer in Python?
flashcards.back: Use int('100'). This returns the integer value 100.

flashcards.front: What will type(3.14) return?
flashcards.back: <class 'float'> — because 3.14 is a floating-point number.

flashcards.front: What is the result of 'Hello' + ' ' + 'World'?
flashcards.back: 'Hello World' — string concatenation joins the strings together.

flashcards.front: What is an f-string in Python?
flashcards.back: A formatted string literal that allows embedding expressions inside string literals. Example: f'Price: R{price:.2f}' where price is a variable.

quizItems.prompt: What data type is the value 3.14?
quizItems.explanation: 3.14 is a decimal number, which Python classifies as a float (floating-point number).

quizItems.prompt: Which function converts a number to a string in Python?
quizItems.explanation: The str() function converts other data types to a string representation.

quizItems.prompt: What is the result of 5 // 2 in Python?
quizItems.explanation: The // operator performs floor division, which returns the integer part of the division result. 5 // 2 = 2.

workedExamples.title: Calculating VAT in Python
workedExamples.summary: Using variables and data types to calculate South African VAT (15%).
workedExamples.problem: A product costs R200. Write Python code to calculate and display the price including 15% VAT.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Assign the price: price = 200.0

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Define the VAT rate: vat_rate = 0.15

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Calculate VAT amount: vat = price * vat_rate

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Calculate total: total = price + vat

steps.label: Step 5
steps.explanation: Display result: print(f'Total price with VAT: R{total:.2f}')

flashcards.front: What is the syntax for an if statement in Python?
How does a for loop work in Python?
flashcards.back: A for loop iterates over a sequence (list, range, string). Syntax: for item in sequence: followed by the indented code block.

flashcards.front: What does range(1, 6) generate?
flashcards.back: The sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. range(start, stop) generates numbers from start up to (but not including) stop.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between break and continue?
flashcards.back: break exits the loop entirely. continue skips the current iteration and moves to the next one.

quizItems.explanation: range(3) generates 0, 1, 2. The loop prints each value on a new line.

quizItems.prompt: Which keyword is used to skip the rest of the current loop iteration and continue with the next?
quizItems.explanation: The continue statement skips the remaining code in the current iteration and proceeds to the next iteration of the loop.

quizItems.prompt: A while loop continues as long as its condition is:
quizItems.explanation: A while loop executes its body repeatedly as long as the condition evaluates to True.

workedExamples.title: Grade Classification
workedExamples.summary: Using if/elif/else to classify a student's mark into a grade category.
workedExamples.problem: Write Python code that takes a student's percentage mark and prints 'Distinction', 'Merit', 'Pass', or 'Fail'.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Get the mark: mark = int(input('Enter mark: '))

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Check for Distinction: if mark >= 75: print('Distinction')

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Check for Merit: elif mark >= 60: print('Merit')

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Check for Pass: elif mark >= 50: print('Pass')

steps.label: Step 5
steps.explanation: Otherwise it's a Fail: else: print('Fail')

workedExamples.answer:
For mark = 82: Distinction
For mark = 65: Merit
For mark = 52: Pass
For mark = 40: Fail

flashcards.front: What is the correct syntax to define a function in Python?
flashcards.back:
def function_name(parameters):
    # function body
    return value
The def keyword is followed by the function name and parentheses.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a local and global variable?
flashcards.back: A local variable is defined inside a function and only accessible within it. A global variable is defined outside functions and accessible throughout the program.

flashcards.front: How do you import the math module and use the square root function?
flashcards.back:
import math
result = math.sqrt(16)  # returns 4.0

flashcards.front: What does the return statement do in a function?
flashcards.back: It sends a value back to the caller and ends the function's execution. A function without a return statement returns None.

quizItems.prompt: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
quizItems.explanation: In Python, functions are defined using the 'def' keyword followed by the function name and parentheses.

quizItems.prompt: What will the function return if it has no return statement?
quizItems.explanation: In Python, a function without a return statement implicitly returns None.

quizItems.prompt: How do you import only the sqrt function from the math module?
quizItems.explanation: The 'from module import function' syntax imports a specific function from a module, allowing you to call it without the module prefix.

workedExamples.title: VAT Calculator Function
workedExamples.summary: Creating a reusable function to calculate VAT-inclusive prices.
workedExamples.problem: Write a Python function called calculate_vat that takes a price and VAT rate as parameters and returns the total price including VAT.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Define the function: def calculate_vat(price, vat_rate=0.15):

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Calculate VAT amount: vat = price * vat_rate

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Calculate total: total = price + vat

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Return the result: return total

steps.label: Step 5
steps.explanation:
Call the function: result = calculate_vat(200)
print(f'R{result:.2f}')

flashcards.front: How do you create a list in Python and access its first element?
flashcards.back:
Create: my_list = [10, 20, 30, 40]
Access first element: my_list[0]  # returns 10
Lists use zero-based indexing.

flashcards.front: How do you add an item to the end of a list?
flashcards.back:
Use the append() method: my_list.append(50)
This adds 50 to the end of the list.

flashcards.front: How do you create a dictionary with a student's name and mark?
flashcards.back:
student = {'name': 'Thabo', 'mark': 75}
Access: student['name']  # returns 'Thabo'

flashcards.front: What is the main difference between a list and a set?
flashcards.back: A list is ordered and allows duplicates. A set is unordered and contains only unique values. Sets are useful for removing duplicates.

flashcards.front: How do you iterate over all key-value pairs in a dictionary?
flashcards.back:
Use .items(): for key, value in my_dict.items():
    print(key, value)

quizItems.prompt: What does my_list[-1] return?
quizItems.explanation: Negative indexing in Python counts from the end. -1 refers to the last element, -2 to the second-last, etc.

quizItems.prompt: Which data structure does NOT allow duplicate values?
quizItems.explanation: A set automatically removes duplicate values and only stores unique elements.

quizItems.prompt: How do you access the value associated with key 'age' in a dictionary named 'person'?
quizItems.explanation: Dictionary values are accessed using square bracket notation with the key name in quotes.

workedExamples.title: Student Marks Analysis
workedExamples.summary: Using a list and dictionary to store and analyse student marks.
workedExamples.problem: Store three students' names and marks in a dictionary, then find the average mark.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Create a dictionary: students = {'Thabo': 72, 'Naledi': 85, 'Johan': 64}

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Extract marks into a list: marks = list(students.values())

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Calculate average: average = sum(marks) / len(marks)

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Print result: print(f'Average mark: {average:.1f}%')

flashcards.front: What are the three modes for opening a file in Python?
flashcards.back: 'r' — read (default), 'w' — write (overwrites), 'a' — append (adds to end). Example: open('file.txt', 'r')

flashcards.front: Why should you use 'with open()' instead of just 'open()'?
flashcards.back: The 'with' statement automatically closes the file after the block executes, even if an error occurs. This prevents file corruption and resource leaks.

flashcards.front: How do you handle a FileNotFoundError in Python?
What Pandas function reads a CSV file into a DataFrame?
flashcards.back: pd.read_csv('filename.csv') — this reads the CSV and returns a DataFrame. You must first import pandas as pd.

quizItems.prompt: Which file mode would you use to add data to an existing file without deleting its contents?
quizItems.explanation: Mode 'a' (append) opens the file and adds new data to the end without overwriting existing content.

quizItems.prompt: What does the try/except block do?
options: It catches and handles runtime errors
quizItems.answer: It catches and handles runtime errors
quizItems.explanation: try/except allows the program to handle exceptions (errors) gracefully instead of crashing.

quizItems.prompt: What does CSV stand for?
quizItems.explanation: CSV (Comma-Separated Values) is a plain text format where each record is on a new line and fields are separated by commas.

workedExamples.title: Reading Sales Data from CSV
workedExamples.summary: Opening a CSV file and calculating total sales using Pandas.
workedExamples.problem: You have a CSV file 'sales.csv' with columns 'product' and 'amount'. Read the file and calculate the total sales amount.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Import pandas: import pandas as pd

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Read the file: df = pd.read_csv('sales.csv')

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Calculate total: total = df['amount'].sum()

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Display result: print(f'Total Sales: R{total:,.2f}')

steps.label: Step 5
steps.explanation: Wrap in try/except to handle missing file gracefully.

workedExamples.answer: Total Sales: R[sum of all amounts in the CSV]

flashcards.front: What is a Pandas DataFrame?
flashcards.back: A two-dimensional, labelled data structure with rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet. Created using pd.DataFrame() or pd.read_csv().

flashcards.front: How do you filter a DataFrame to show only rows where 'sales' > 1000?
flashcards.back:
df[df['sales'] > 1000]
This uses boolean indexing to return rows satisfying the condition.

flashcards.front: What does df.groupby('region')['sales'].sum() do?
flashcards.back: It groups the DataFrame by the 'region' column and calculates the total (sum) of 'sales' for each region.

flashcards.front: How do you remove rows with missing values in Pandas?
flashcards.back: Use df.dropna() to remove all rows with any NaN values. Use df.fillna(value) to replace NaN with a specific value.

flashcards.front: What does df.describe() return?
flashcards.back: Summary statistics for all numeric columns: count, mean, std, min, 25th percentile, median, 75th percentile, and max.

quizItems.prompt: Which Pandas function reads a CSV file into a DataFrame?
quizItems.explanation: pd.read_csv() is the standard Pandas function for reading CSV files into a DataFrame.

quizItems.prompt: What does NaN represent in Pandas?
quizItems.explanation: NaN (Not a Number) is used in Pandas to represent missing data points in a dataset.

quizItems.prompt: Which method returns descriptive statistics of a DataFrame?
quizItems.explanation: df.describe() returns summary statistics (count, mean, std, min, max, percentiles) for numeric columns.

workedExamples.title: Regional Sales Analysis with Groupby
workedExamples.summary: Using Pandas groupby to summarise sales data by region.
workedExamples.problem: Given a sales DataFrame with columns 'region', 'product', and 'sales', find the total sales per region and identify the top-performing region.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.explanation: Import and load: import pandas as pd; df = pd.read_csv('sales.csv')

steps.label: Step 2
steps.explanation: Group by region: regional_sales = df.groupby('region')['sales'].sum()

steps.label: Step 3
steps.explanation: Sort descending: regional_sales = regional_sales.sort_values(ascending=False)

steps.label: Step 4
steps.explanation: Find top region: top_region = regional_sales.index[0]

steps.label: Step 5
steps.explanation: Print result: print(f'Top region: {top_region} with R{regional_sales.iloc[0]:,.2f}')

workedExamples.answer: Top region: [region name] with R[highest sales amount]

flashcards.front: How do you import Matplotlib and create a basic line chart?
flashcards.back:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(x_values, y_values)
plt.show()

flashcards.front: How do you add a title and axis labels to a Matplotlib chart?
flashcards.back:
plt.title('My Chart')
plt.xlabel('X Axis Label')
plt.ylabel('Y Axis Label')

flashcards.front: What is the difference between plt.show() and plt.savefig()?
flashcards.back: plt.show() displays the chart on screen. plt.savefig('chart.png') saves it to a file. Use savefig() before show() to avoid saving a blank image.

flashcards.front: Which Matplotlib function creates a bar chart?
flashcards.back:
plt.bar(x_categories, y_values)
For horizontal bars use plt.barh(). Useful for comparing categorical data like sales by province.

quizItems.prompt: Which function creates a scatter plot in Matplotlib?
quizItems.explanation: plt.scatter(x, y) creates a scatter plot showing individual data points, useful for identifying correlations.

quizItems.prompt: What is the correct order of operations to save a Matplotlib chart?
quizItems.explanation: plt.savefig() must be called before plt.show(), because plt.show() clears the figure. Calling savefig() after show() would save a blank image.

quizItems.prompt: How do you create two subplots side by side in Matplotlib?
quizItems.explanation: plt.subplot(rows, cols, index) creates a subplot grid. subplot(1,2,1) is the first plot in a 1-row, 2-column grid; subplot(1,2,2) is the second.

teacherNotes: Module overview: Data Analysis and Programming 222 (BCom, North-West University). This study-guide was auto-generated from the module outline and should be reviewed against the current year's official module guide before use. Pair every chapter with the reference list (see 'referenceList') so students can read the primary/standard source.
Chapter-by-chapter teaching focus (derived from the module's own learning outcomes and key definitions):

• Chapter 1 — Python Basics & Environment. Emphasise: Install Python and set up a development environment (Anaconda/VS Code); Write and execute basic Python scripts; Understand the difference between script mode and interactive mode. Local context: NWU BCom students typically use Anaconda with Jupyter Notebooks or VS Code as their Python environment. Python is increasingly used in South African business analytics contexts, including financial modelling and data reporting.

• Chapter 2 — Data Types & Variables. Emphasise: Identify Python's core data types: int, float, str, bool; Declare and assign variables following naming conventions; Perform type conversion using int(), float(), str(). Local context: Understanding data types is fundamental for processing South African business data such as rand amounts (float), customer IDs (int or str), and boolean flags in business rule systems.

• Chapter 3 — Control Flow. Emphasise: Write conditional logic using if, elif, and else; Implement for loops to iterate over sequences; Use while loops for condition-based repetition. Local context: Control flow structures are used in business logic programming, such as applying VAT conditionally on South African transactions or iterating through customer records to calculate balances.

• Chapter 4 — Functions & Modules. Emphasise: Define and call functions with parameters and return values; Understand variable scope (local vs global); Import and use built-in Python modules. Local context: Functions promote code reusability, which is essential in business data processing tasks such as repeatedly calculating tax (15% VAT) or formatting South African rand values.

• Chapter 5 — Data Structures (Lists/Dicts/Sets). Emphasise: Create and manipulate Python lists using indexing and methods; Build and access dictionaries using key-value pairs; Use sets for unique collections and set operations. Local context: Data structures are used to organise business data such as lists of product prices, dictionaries of customer details, and sets of unique transaction IDs in South African retail analytics.

• Chapter 6 — File I/O & Data Handling. Emphasise: Open, read, and write text files using Python's open() function; Read and write CSV files using the csv module and Pandas; Handle exceptions using try/except blocks. Local context: File handling is critical for processing business data files such as CSV exports from South African accounting systems (Pastel, Sage) or government datasets from Stats SA.

• Chapter 7 — Pandas & Data Analysis. Emphasise: Create and manipulate Pandas Series and DataFrames; Filter, sort, and index data in a DataFrame; Perform groupby operations and aggregation. Local context: Pandas is widely used for analysing South African business datasets such as JSE stock data, Stats SA survey results, and SARS tax return data.

• Chapter 8 — Data Visualisation (Matplotlib). Emphasise: Create line, bar, and scatter plots using Matplotlib; Customise plots with titles, axis labels, legends, and colours; Create subplots to display multiple charts. Local context: Data visualisation is essential for communicating business insights to South African stakeholders. Charts are used in BCom business reports, marketing dashboards, and economic policy presentations.
